first_answers.nemo:
The energy cost to transfer an electron from A to B is the ionization potential of A minus the electron affinity of B: \(5.5 \text{ eV} - 1.5 \text{ eV} = 4.0 \text{ eV}\). For an energetically stable ionic bond, the Coulomb attraction energy must at least compensate this cost. The Coulomb energy is \(-\frac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r}\), where \(r = r_{A^+} + r_{B^-}\) and \(\frac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \approx 1.44 \text{ eV·nm}\). Setting \(\frac{1.44}{r} \ge 4.0 \text{ eV}\) gives \(r \le 0.36 \text{ nm}\). Given \(r_{B^-} = 0.20 \text{ nm}\), the maximum radius of \(A^+\) is \(0.36 - 0.20 = 0.16 \text{ nm}\).

ANSWER: J
